core_obligations: Set up a minimal counterexample (proof line 20419 with the paragraphs): assume the map is not an isomorphism for some point z of Y x_K X and argue by induction on dim(X) + dim(Y), so that a counterexample with minimal dimension sum is chosen.

Rule out positive transcendence degree over X (proof lines 20436-20484): if the image x of z in X has positive transcendence degree over K, the strictly henselian local ring at x has dimension at least one, and the stalk computation together with the vanishing of the cohomology of torsion sheaves of invertible order on a curve forces the base change map to be an isomorphism at z, contradicting the choice of counterexample.

Rule out positive transcendence degree over Y (proof lines 20487-20533): the same argument with the roles of the two factors exchanged rules out the case where the image of z in Y has positive transcendence degree over K.

Conclude by independence (proof lines 20536-20549): hence both images of z are closed points of X and of Y over K, so the relevant fibres are zero-dimensional and the map is an isomorphism there, which contradicts the existence of a counterexample and proves the statement.
The author's last paragraph (proof lines 20552-20594) records the same argument in the form in which the statement of the lemma is applied elsewhere, closing the proof.
proof_roadmap: Choose a counterexample with minimal dim(X) + dim(Y).
If the point maps to a point of X of positive transcendence degree over K, reduce to the known vanishing on a curve and get an isomorphism.
If instead its image in Y has positive transcendence degree, exchange the roles.
In the remaining case both images are closed points, where the base change map is an isomorphism; contradiction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves base change for an open immersion in the Kunneth setting: for K a field, j : U -> X an open immersion of K-schemes of finite type, Y of finite type over K and F an abelian sheaf on U_etale with torsion stalks of orders invertible in K, the base change map q^{-1}Rj_*F -> Rh_*p^{-1}F is an isomorphism (statement lines 20402-20417). The proof is a minimal-counterexample argument on dim(X) + dim(Y) with two nontrivial reductions: a point with positive transcendence degree over X is handled by a stalk computation at the strictly henselian local ring together with the vanishing of cohomology of torsion sheaves of invertible order on a curve (proof lines 20436-20484), and the symmetric situation over Y is excluded in the same way with the roles exchanged (proof lines 20487-20533); what remains is a point whose images are closed points, where the comparison is immediate (proof lines 20536-20549). The non-formal content is the combination of the two reductions with the dimension induction. The claim is H2: a long but completely written-out argument whose only external input is the vanishing statement for curves.
